How long does it take from Bangkok to Koh Samui? | About 3–4 hours door to door by direct flight (1h05–1h15 in the air), 5–7 hours via a low-cost flight to Surat Thani and the ferry, and 11.5–17 hours by bus-and-boat or night train.
What is the cheapest way from Bangkok to Koh Samui? | A government coach from the Southern Bus Terminal or Mo Chit with the Seatran ferry costs about 620–960 THB at the counter and takes 12–16 hours.
Is the night train to Surat Thani worth it? | Yes if you have time: Express 85 leaves Krung Thep Aphiwat at 19:50 and reaches Surat Thani at 06:23, a 2nd-class berth costs about 755–825 THB, and you are on Samui by late morning.
Which Bangkok airport has flights to Samui? | Both: Suvarnabhumi has about 20–25 Bangkok Airways flights a day and Don Mueang about 3; low-cost flights to Surat Thani leave mainly from Don Mueang.
Can I buy one ticket from Bangkok to Samui by bus and boat? | Yes, Lomprayah (1,250–1,750 THB) and Boonsiri (about 1,450 THB) sell bus-plus-catamaran tickets from Khao San Road, and government coaches sell tickets including the Seatran ferry.
Can I drive from Bangkok to Koh Samui? | Yes, it is roughly 650–700 km to Donsak pier, then about 1.5 hours on the Seatran or Raja car ferry; check that your rental contract allows ferry crossings.
How far in advance should I book flights to Samui? | Book 6–10 weeks ahead for December–January, Chinese New Year, Songkran and July–August, and 2–4 weeks ahead at other times; fares rarely drop at the last minute.
Can I go from Bangkok to Koh Phangan via Samui? | Yes, fly to Samui, take a 5–10 minute taxi to the Bangrak piers or Big Buddha pier, and catch a 20–50 minute boat to Thong Sala or Haad Rin.
